visualReview.notes: Inspected all seven final portable views against four individually viewed local 2008–2010 museum, bar, lower-range and road-frontage originals. Five-window slate-hung main range, twin chimneys, perpendicular granite museum wing, eaves dormers and gabled entrances remain distinct. Review corrected shallow dormers, overly uniform stonework and the lower-range entrance.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all seven final shared-material views including the footprint overlay and full front. Granite, roof slate and timber use shared metric surfaces; slate-hung wall cladding and glass are separate local materials. Flat ground is a material fixture; portable views retain independent terrain.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all nineteen final lighting, quality and forced-detail views. Skyline retains the principal ranges, roofs and chimneys; district restores openings and porches; street and closeup restore leaded casements, dormers and masonry courses. Synthetic neighbors are style fixtures. No physical-device performance measurement is claimed.

geographicReview.notes: Mapped combined inn/hotel outline is retained as evidence; explicit scope cuts exclude the long modern east hotel and far rear service wing. Anchor [-4.5667,50.5623], heading 0.742: +X northeast along the main bar, +Z southeast toward the forecourt. Independent unmodified Terrarium elevations use datum 279.0506 m at forecourt [4,9.5]. Foundations extend to -3 m. Footprint-relative range includes the excluded modern mapped areas; footprint suppression remains off.

fidelityReview.scope: Historic Jamaica Inn bar, museum/stables wing, lower east connector and attached rear range; modern hotel extensions and interiors excluded.
fidelityReview.notes: Four individually inspected Qualla originals, Historic England architectural description and satellite roof context control the facade and range arrangement. Heights, hidden rear elevations, roof joins, stone bond and fine ornament remain approximations. The distinctive main facade and chimney shafts are slate-hung; museum walls are exposed granite. No photo pixels or exact sign lettering copied.

runtimeLodReview.notes: All four current levels were visually inspected and pass budgets; exact triangle and byte counts are recorded in levels. Error values are authoring budgets, not measured deviations.

geometryValidation.notes: Exact regeneration, ordinary import verification, four current LOD checks and strict medium-fi audit passed. Source bundle, scene and terrain schemas pass; independent terrain PNG encoding error is recorded above. No independent Khronos-validator run is claimed.

limitations: Original medium-fi exterior based on individually inspected local 2008–2010 photographs, Historic England architectural description and mapped roof layout.

Main facade and axial chimneys are slate-hung; original geometry and color courses represent this distinct cladding. Shared granite, roof slate and timber surfaces are bound; glass and vertical slate cladding use separate local materials.
Modern long east hotel wing and far rear service wing excluded. Rear elevations, roof joins, heights and fine stonework remain approximate; interiors, signs and temporary furniture excluded.
Independent Terrarium elevations are preserved without flattening; ground contact and foundations remain host-dependent rather than surveyed.
